quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit can
Alcohol does not
Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
Only a blood alcohol level greater than 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol reduces your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving ability will suffer. You cannot drink and drive safely.

questions.question: You are driving behind a motorcycle and want to pass. You must:

options.text: Stay in the right lane as much as possible because the motorcycle is small and doesn't use all of the lane.
Blow your horn to make the motorcycle move onto the shoulder so that you can pass.
Have your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: When passing a motorcycle, give it a full lane. Never share the same lane with a motorcycle. Returning to your lane too soon can force the rider to swerve right into traffic or off the road.

questions.question: A sign with this shape means:

options.text: No passing zone.
Right turn permitted on red.
Yield right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: A pennant-shaped sign shows the start of a no passing zone.

questions.question: If you are turning onto a street with more than one lane traveling in your direction, you should:

options.text: Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane.
Turn into the lane marked with an arrow.
Turn into the middle lane.
Turn into any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes in your direction, turn into the lane nearest to where you came from. Do not change lanes while turning.

questions.question: To avoid collisions with vehicles in your blind spots, you should:

options.text: Quickly turn your head to see if your blind spot is clear before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Quickly turn your head to see if your blind spot is clear before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: When approaching a flashing red traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Drive through the intersection if there is no crossing traffic.
Continue driving, as they have the right-of-way.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the light like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the light like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights mark dangerous intersections. Treat them the same as stop signs.

questions.question: It is best to keep a space cushion:

options.text: Only in back of your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Only in front of the vehicle.
On all sides of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your vehicle on all sides so you have time to react to hazards. Do not crowd vehicles to your left and right.

questions.question: If there is a deep puddle on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Maintain the posted speed to make it through the water.
Avoid the puddle if possible.
Shift into neutral as you drive through the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the puddle if possible.
questions.explanation: To prevent skidding, avoid slippery areas like ice, wet leaves, oil, and deep puddles. A dry, solid surface is safest for driving.

questions.question: Compared to driving during the day, driving at night is:

options.text: Less dangerous.
No more or less dangerous.
More dangerous.
Easier on your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous than day driving. It is harder to see, headlights can blind you, and more tired or impaired drivers are on the road.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly blows out while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.
Pump the brakes rapidly.
Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: If your tire blows out, do not panic. Hold the steering wheel firmly and release the accelerator so the car slows down. Apply the brakes gently once the car has slowed. Wait until the car is moving slowly before moving to the road shoulder.

questions.question: You are in a minor collision at an intersection. No one is hurt and there is very little damage. What should you do?

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if you can do so safely.
Do not move your vehicle for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: After a collision with no injuries, move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?

options.text: New drivers
Human error
Bad weather
Bad roads

questions.correctAnswerText: Human error
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do not see other vehicles or do something unexpected. Talk to other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?

options.text: In an intersection if there are no oncoming vehicles
Wherever signs or road markings allow passing
In a curve if there are no oncoming vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever signs or road markings allow passing
questions.explanation: Never pass in intersections, parking lots, or alleys. Never pass on curves or hills where you cannot see ahead. Only pass where signs or road markings say it is safe. Make sure you have enough space to pass safely.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right
The driver on the left
One driver may continue without stopping
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right
questions.explanation: If you arrive at an open intersection at the same time as a vehicle to your right, let that vehicle go first. You can then go when it is safe.

questions.question: You are coming to a railroad crossing with flashing signals. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the vehicle ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing signals at a railroad crossing, stop your vehicle at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. Watch for a lowered gate or listen for a train.

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, you must:

options.text: Yield to traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.
Yield only to vehicles on your right
Slow down but never stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, let traffic in the lanes you want to enter go first. Be ready to stop, but you can go if there are no other vehicles coming.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on a wet road?

options.text: As you drive faster, your tires grip the road less.
Water does not affect cars with good tires
Shallow water is more dangerous than deep water
Slower speeds make the road more slippery

questions.correctAnswerText: As you drive faster, your tires grip the road less.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on a wet road, the less your tires grip it. If you go too fast, your tires can lose contact with the road and you may hydroplane or slide.

questions.question: A steady green light means you:

options.text: Must slow down and get ready to stop
Must stop and check for oncoming traffic
May drive through if the road is clear
Cannot turn right

questions.correctAnswerText: May drive through if the road is clear
questions.explanation: A steady green light lets you drive through the intersection if it is clear. You can also turn right or left unless a sign says you cannot. Yield to other vehicles and pedestrians when turning.

questions.question: When you enter a roadway from a private road, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other drivers
Stop with part of your car on the road to alert drivers
Drive out fast to merge with traffic
Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, let pedestrians and traffic go first.

questions.question: You do not need to keep as much distance behind a motorcycle as behind a car.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can stop faster than cars. Keep three to four seconds of distance behind a motorcycle so the rider has time to react in an emergency.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided multilane highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as quickly as you can.
Slow down, move to give the emergency vehicle a clear path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to give the emergency vehicle a clear path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights, slow down and move your vehicle to create a clear path. Then stop. Do not try to speed ahead of the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Very uncommon.
Extremely dangerous.
Not a serious concern.
Just as safe as normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Extremely dangerous.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is extremely dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers at risk. Paying full attention to the road helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Stop sign ahead.
Divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn in the direction the arrow points. In this case, you cannot turn right.

questions.question: When can you legally block an intersection?

options.text: If you entered on a green light.
During rush hour traffic.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You may not block an intersection, even if the light is green. Only enter the intersection if you can cross completely before the light turns red. Blocking an intersection is illegal and you can be cited.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, start your turn from:

options.text: Any lane (if it is safe).
The lane closest to the left curb.
The center lane of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, begin your turn from the far left lane.
